subject: environmental-science
title: Renewables, EROI and Capacity Factors
welcome_lead: From sunbeams to gigawatts — quantify the energy returned on energy invested.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on renewable energy, capacity factors and EROI.
final_note: Capacity factor and EROI separate marketing hype from real net energy.

concepts.def: Ratio of actual energy output to maximum possible over a period (e.g., wind ~30–45%).
Energy returned on energy invested — net energy yield ratio.
Photovoltaic conversion of light to electricity; capacity factor ~10–25%.
Kinetic energy of moving air harnessed by turbines; offshore CF ~40–55%.
Gravitational potential of water converted to electricity; CF ~30–60%.
Lifetime cost per unit of energy ($/MWh), enabling like-for-like comparison.

walkthroughs.body_html: A 1 MW turbine running 35% CF delivers 0.35 MW average. CF varies with resource, technology and grid curtailment.
Hydro EROI often >50; wind ~20; solar PV ~10. Oil EROI fell from ~100 in 1930 to ~15 today as accessible reserves deplete.
Storage (batteries, pumped hydro), demand response and continental interconnection smooth variable renewables.

options: Actual energy output divided by maximum possible output

mcqs.q: Why does renewable energy require energy storage solutions?
options: Renewable energy can never meet demand.
Because they generate too much energy.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Solar and wind generation are intermittent - storage smooths out supply and demand.

mcqs.q: How do greenhouse gases warm Earth?
options: They block heat from escaping into space (like a literal lid).
They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
They absorb infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface and re-radiate some back down.
Because polar bears help spread heat.

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
Because warming is positive (a good thing).
